rationale: M60/#924 (the cpp row of the R10 name-surface class, landed from the census's own files). The cpp analyzer extracted the include name as `text.slice(text.indexOf("include") + 7)` over the WHOLE preproc_include node — so every trailing comment became part of the published module and of the include_dependency edge target: `#include <vector> // vector` published `vector // vector`. MEASURED through the production entry on the two pinned cpp corpora (script/m14/tmp/c924-include-ab.ts, fmt + nlohmann-json, 71 files, 1,567 published names): 876 of them carried whitespace, 438 include sites, all of them comment-glue; after the fix 4 remain and all four are a DIFFERENT class (`operator"" _json` user-defined-literal names, not includes). The A/B is one-directional: 724 distinct names renamed, 568 clean names gained, and 0 removed names whose comment-stripped form did not appear — no include was lost. The same block reported system-ness as `includePath.startsWith("<")` on the STRIPPED name, where stripIncludeChars has already deleted the `<`, so no cpp include could ever be reported as a system one; both metadata fields now read the raw path node, which is what the C lane's getIncludePath has always done. The extraction is structural now (the `path` field, literal-only like C-D2), so the fixture also pins that a macro-COMPOSED argument publishes nothing — the c/macro-composed-include contract, previously unpinned for cpp. **Reverting mutant: `cpp/include-name-comment-glue`** (mutate-analyzer.ts) restores the text slice; this fixture is the only one that catches it.  M14 ONTOLOGY (2026-10-04): the include rows are now `imports` — C++'s file inclusion is a first-class `imports` edge, the same kind and metadata the C lane emits for the identical construct (c/macro-composed-include; reverted by the `c/include-kind-downgraded` mutant). The PRE-FIX rows in `forbidRelationships` move WITH the kind on purpose: a revert of the name extraction now produces an `imports` row whose target carries the comment glue, so a forbid row still written as `references` would not catch the revert it exists to catch. The `references` label on the CLEAN targets is forbidden separately, so a silent relabel back to `references` fails this fixture too.

expectImports.comment: `#include <vector>  // vector` on line 25 — the module is the path node's text, and `<...>` makes it a system include (before the fix this was `vector  // vector`, and isSystemInclude was false for every cpp include).
`#include "local_header.h"    /* local */` on line 26 — the block comment is not part of the name either, and a quoted include is not a system one.

expectRelationships.note: the include_dependency edge carries the same corrected name; M59.A7 (#825) puts the row on the PATH node's line.

THE TARGET IS NOW PINNED, BECAUSE IT IS NOW STABLE. It was left unconstrained while it was a PATH - a path varies with the checkout, and pinning one would have made the fixture a test of the machine. It is now the part's MODULE SYMBOL (its file stem), the same on every machine and the only form the arbiter can bind: MEASURED path => 0 resolved of 4,612 and symbol => 383 resolved of 4,612, same population, same 2,000-file stride sample, the target's FORM the only variable. A CONSTRAINT THAT CAN NOW BE PINNED IS A CHECK THAT SHOULD NOW BE OWNED, so this fixture asserts the stem itself rather than merely that some part_of row exists.
